experiment: live A6 native recovery: m1 Gazebo scan -> hdl tracking; loss -> finest BBS candidates over 2 recent scans, prior-guided -> A6 backend -> native hdl /initialpose -> new lease
native_service_used: hdl /initialpose (reset); hdl /relocalize single-candidate service covered by R1078
input_semantics: sensor-local scan relabelled base_link, voxel .3; Gazebo truth scoring only

candidate_source.node: .1 BBS (map data .2, grid .1, query .2, scan z -.5..6, full m1 PCD)
candidate_source.selection: nearest to last healthy /hdl_odom within prior radius 1.5 m

negative_control: empty scan -> all BBS queries return no candidate -> supervisor deadline -> FAILED, command_allowed=false, no /initialpose
findings: coarse-resolution majority can override the correct fine candidate; at (0,1) the coarse .5/.2 pair sat near 1.0 m while the fine .1 candidate was 0.0-0.2 m, so recovery now trusts the finest candidate with a short-horizon prior
BBS on a single rotating scan flips basins; two recent scans plus prior radius 1.5 m removed the observed 0.6-4.3 m flips
a third BBS query could hang past the 20 s deadline; two scans keep the recovery inside the deadline
supervisor startup (INITIALIZING) no longer triggers relocalize; --initial-lease allows a known healthy lease to be restored
candidate/backend messages now carry yaw; the native /initialpose reset applies the BBS orientation
fed clouds use monotonic sim stamps, avoiding E_LOC_STAMP_NONMONOTONIC after reset
limits: static simulation, 3 spawn poses, 1-2 cycles, no motion/real robot; prior-guided recovery assumes the last healthy pose bounds a short outage, so kidnapped/long-outage recovery is not covered; GT posthoc only; A6 remains PARTIAL
